knowledgePattern: Test both halves of a divisibility counterexample
solution:
A counterexample must have 12∣N2 but 12∤N. For N=6, N2=36 is divisible by 12 while 6 is not. For N=8, the square 64 is not divisible by 12, so the premise fails.

For N=18, the square 324 is divisible by 12 while 18 is not. For N=24, both the square and the original number are divisible by 12, so this supports the implication rather than refuting it.

Exactly I and III are counterexamples. Answer D.

hints.title: Require a true premise and a false conclusion
hints.body: For each proposed N, make two checks: whether its square is divisible by 12, and whether N itself is divisible by 12.
hints.recap: A counterexample satisfies every hypothesis and violates the conclusion.
hints.pitfall: A number failing the hypothesis cannot refute the implication.
hints.pause: Complete the two checks for all four values, then select the matching option.
